doc.summary: Finds and returns a prioritized sharpening or weight stone based on the weapon's subclass type.
doc.overview: This function attempts to locate an appropriate consumable stone for a given weapon by first checking if the input weapon is valid. It then inspects the weapon's template to determine its subclass, specifically distinguishing between sword/axe/dagger/polearm types and mace/staff/fist types. Depending on this classification, it iterates through predefined lists of prioritized stone IDs to find a matching consumable item.

params.name: weapon
params.desc: Pointer to the weapon item for which a sharpening or weight stone is being sought.

doc.notes: Returns nullptr if the weapon is invalid, lacks a template, or no matching stone exists in the game world. The function relies on internal static arrays of stone IDs that are hardcoded for specific weapon categories.

doc.summary: Finds the highest-priority consumable oil item for a specific bot class and specialization.
doc.overview: This function searches for an available oil item based on the bot's class and special tab, prioritizing specific oil types according to predefined lists. It iterates through the selected priority list, calling FindConsumable to locate the first existing item of that type before returning it or nullptr if none are found.

params.name: weapon
params.desc: The weapon item associated with the bot; used to determine the bot's class and specialization.

doc.returns: Item* (pointer to the found oil item or nullptr)
doc.notes: Relies on FindConsumable for existence checks; returns nullptr if weapon is null, item template is missing, or no prioritized oils are available.

doc.summary: Retrieves a vector of pointers to all inventory, equipped, and keyring items for the specified bot.
doc.overview: This function aggregates item data from four distinct storage locations within the bot's inventory system: the bag slots, general item slots, the keyring, and equipped gear. It iterates through each defined slot range using predefined constants to identify valid items via the bot's internal retrieval methods, collecting them into a single vector for subsequent processing.
doc.notes: The function relies on the existence of the `bot` object in the current scope and assumes all slot constants are correctly defined. It does not modify any global state or perform I/O operations.

doc.overview: This function iterates through three distinct inventory regions: the bag slots, item slots, and keyring slots. For each region, it queries the bot for items at specific positions and adds them to a result vector if they exist. The implementation relies on predefined slot constants to determine the range of indices to check.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot object is valid before invoking this function, as it accesses bot->GetItemByPos. The returned vector may contain duplicate item pointers if an item exists in multiple slot types (though logically unlikely for a single item instance). Edge case: If no items are present in any inventory region, an empty vector is returned.

doc.summary: Returns the total quantity of items with a specific ID across all inventory slots, bags, and keyrings for the bot.
doc.overview: This function iterates through three distinct inventory regions: bag slots, item slots, and keyring slots to search for items matching the provided itemId. For every match found in these locations, it accumulates the item's count into a running total before returning the final sum. The implementation relies on direct memory access via bot pointers and assumes valid slot ranges defined by macro constants.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item type to search for within the bot's inventory.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the itemId is valid to avoid unnecessary iteration; edge cases include bots with empty inventories or items located exclusively in keyrings which are included in the search.

doc.summary: Checks whether a specific item ID exists anywhere within the bot's inventory, bag, or keyring.
doc.overview: This function iterates through three distinct storage locations: the main inventory slots, the bag container, and the keyring. It retrieves items from each location using the bot's internal state and compares their template IDs against the provided itemId to determine existence.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to search for within the bot's inventory.

doc.notes: Relies on the bot object being valid and populated; returns false if no matching item is found in any checked location.

doc.summary: Retrieves a list of active quests from the bot's quest log that require a specific item ID.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the bot's current quest log to identify which quests are currently active and contain a requirement for the provided item. It returns a vector containing pairs of pointers to the Quest template objects and their corresponding required item IDs, allowing callers to easily determine if an item is needed for any ongoing quest.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to search for within active quests.

doc.notes: Returns an empty vector if itemId is zero or no active quests require the specified item. The function relies on external state from sObjectMgr and bot, so it assumes those objects are properly initialized.

doc.summary: Imbues a specific item with the Shadow AI's unique properties and visual effects.
doc.overview: This function applies the Shadow AI's special attributes to a given item by invoking an internal helper with default target flags and an empty object GUID. It is typically called during item creation or modification to ensure the item behaves correctly within the Shadow faction context.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the Item instance that will receive the imbued properties.

doc.notes: The function internally calls ImbueItem with TARGET_FLAG_NONE and ObjectGuid::Empty, effectively bypassing target-specific logic for this operation.

doc.summary: Imbues a specified item onto a target unit by delegating the actual imbuing logic to the core system.
doc.overview: This function serves as a high-level wrapper that validates the presence of a target unit before proceeding. It extracts the unique GUID of the target and invokes the primary ImbueItem implementation with the appropriate TARGET_FLAG_UNIT context, ensuring the item is correctly associated with the unit's identity.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the item instance that will be imbued onto the target.

params.name: target
params.desc: Pointer to the unit instance intended to receive the imbued item.

doc.notes: If target is null, the function returns immediately without performing any operations. Callers should ensure target validity before invoking this wrapper to avoid unnecessary processing.

doc.summary: Imbues a specified item into the target inventory slot by checking for an existing item and applying the imbue effect.
doc.overview: This function attempts to apply an imbue effect from a source item to a specific slot in the bot's inventory bag. It first validates that the target slot is within valid equipment bounds, then retrieves the item at that location if it exists. If a valid target item is found, the imbue operation is executed using the source item and the target item's GUID.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the source item that will be imbued into the target slot.

params.name: targetInventorySlot
params.desc: The index of the inventory slot where the item should be placed, limited to equipment slots.

doc.notes: Returns early if the target slot is invalid or empty; callers must ensure the source item is valid before invoking this function.

doc.summary: Imbues an item by constructing a CMSG_USE_ITEM packet containing the item's template spell data and optional target information.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the primary spell ID from an item's template and constructs a WorldPacket for the CMSG_USE_ITEM command. It serializes the item's bag slot, equipment slot, cast count, spell ID, GUID, glyph index, and cast flags into the packet before queuing it for delivery to the server.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the Item object to be imbued.

params.name: targetFlag
params.desc: Bitmask indicating the type of target (UNIT, ITEM, or GAMEOBJECT).

params.name: targetGUID
params.desc: The GUID of the target if a specific target is required.

doc.notes: Calls bot->GetSession()->QueuePacket to send the packet; assumes item pointer is valid as it returns early if null.

doc.summary: EnchantItemT applies a specific enchantment to an item in the player's inventory bag based on spell ID and slot.
doc.overview: This function retrieves an item from the specified slot in the bot's inventory bag and checks if it is valid, owned by a player present in the world, and has an active session. It then verifies that the target spell exists and is compatible with the item's subclass and inventory type before applying the enchantment.

params.name: spellid
params.desc: The unique identifier of the spell to be applied as an enchantment.

params.name: slot
params.desc: The index of the item slot within the inventory bag (INVENTORY_SLOT_BAG_0).

doc.notes: Calls GetItemByPos and ApplyEnchantment; relies on spell compatibility masks and player session validity.

doc.summary: Returns the count of raid members with a specific aura on the specified player.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all members of the bot's group, filtering for players currently in the world and sharing the same raid as the target player. It then checks each valid member for the presence of the named spell aura and increments a counter if found. The final count is returned to the caller.

params.name: dis
params.desc: The maximum distance threshold (in game units) to consider a group member as 'near'.

doc.notes: Excludes the bot itself from the count; assumes valid bot object context.

doc.summary: Determines if a bot unit is currently allowed to move based on vehicle status, combat states, and movement type.
doc.overview: The CanMove function evaluates whether a specific bot unit can initiate or continue movement by checking for various disabling conditions. It first verifies that the unit is not inside a vehicle, then checks for frozen, dead (non-ghost), teleported, or under aura effects such as root, polymorph, confusion, charm, stun, or flight states. Finally, it confirms the unit's current motion generator type is not set to flight.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking this function. Edge cases include units transitioning between states like death or vehicle entry, which may cause rapid state changes.

doc.summary: Appends a queued chat reply to the internal response queue for later processing.
doc.overview: This function accepts a ChatQueuedReply object and moves it into the global chatReplies vector, ensuring efficient memory transfer without copying. It serves as the entry point for adding user-generated or system messages to the ShadowAI's message buffer before they are dispatched to clients. The operation is non-blocking and assumes the caller has already validated the reply content.

params.name: chatReply
params.desc: The chat reply object containing the message text, sender ID, timestamp, and priority level.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the ChatQueuedReply is fully constructed before passing it to this function. The function relies on std::move semantics; if the object is used elsewhere after this call, undefined behavior may occur.

doc.summary: Compares two strings for equality after converting both to lowercase.
doc.overview: This function performs a case-insensitive comparison of two input strings by first checking if their lengths match, then iterating through each character to verify they are identical when converted to lowercase. It returns true only if all characters correspond exactly in the lowercased form; otherwise, it immediately returns false upon finding a mismatch.

params.name: s1
params.desc: The first string to compare.

params.name: s2
params.desc: The second string to compare.

doc.notes: Caller should ensure strings are null-terminated if using C-style functions internally, though std::string handles this safely. Edge case: empty strings of equal length will correctly return true.

doc.summary: Validates whether a bot can equip an item into a specific inventory slot, returning an error code if any constraint is violated.
doc.overview: This function performs a comprehensive check on various game mechanics and item properties to determine if a bot can successfully equip a given item. It verifies ownership, loot status, level requirements, and equipment slot availability while accounting for special cases like dual-wielding limits and unique item restrictions. The function returns an InventoryResult indicating success or the specific reason for failure.

params.name: slot
params.desc: The target inventory slot index where the item should be equipped.

params.name: dest
params.desc: An output parameter that receives the actual slot index if the item is successfully equipped, otherwise remains 0.

params.name: pItem
params.desc: Pointer to the Item instance being evaluated for equipping.

params.name: swap
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether the item should be swapped into an existing slot if one is available.

params.name: not_loading
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether the bot is currently in a loading state, affecting certain equipment checks.

doc.notes: The function relies on external scripts via sScriptMgr->OnPlayerCanEquipItem and performs deep checks on item templates, bot capabilities (dual-wield, titan grip), and inventory constraints. It handles edge cases such as limited ammo pouches, specific weapon types requiring two-handed grips, and simultaneous equipment of similar items.

doc.summary: Determines the valid equipment slots for a given item template and optionally swaps them based on dual-wielding capability.
doc.overview: This function maps an item's inventory type to its corresponding equipment slot(s), handling complex cases like dual-wielding, polearms, and class-specific relic placements. It initializes a fixed-size array of four slots and populates it based on the item's template properties, such as subclass and inventory type. The 'swap' parameter allows callers to request an alternative slot configuration if the primary option is unavailable.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to the ItemTemplate structure defining the item's properties like inventory type and subclass.

params.name: slot
params.desc: The specific equipment slot index being queried or validated (e.g., NULL_SLOT, EQUIPMENT_SLOT_MAINHAND).

params.name: swap
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to attempt swapping the primary slot with an alternative if the first is invalid.

doc.notes: The function relies on external bot state (dual-wielding ability, class context) for certain item types like weapons and relics. It does not perform I/O or modify global server state.

doc.summary: Returns true if the provided player is on the same map and instance as the bot and is not currently being teleported.
doc.overview: This function checks whether a specific player is in a valid state to be targeted by the Shadow AI bot. It verifies that the player exists, shares the same map ID and instance ID as the bot, and ensures the player is not undergoing teleportation.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object to evaluate.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure player pointer is non-null before calling; returns false if player does not match bot's map or instance context.

doc.summary: Verifies if a WorldObject is safe to interact with by checking map and instance alignment, player status, and teleportation state.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a given object can be safely targeted or acted upon by the bot. It first ensures the object exists and shares the same map and instance ID as the bot, then specifically checks that if the object is a player, they are not currently being teleported.

params.name: obj
params.desc: Pointer to the WorldObject to evaluate for safety.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure obj is not null before passing it, though the function performs a null check internally. Edge case: Returns false if obj is a player who is in the process of being teleported.

doc.summary: Retrieves the appropriate chat channel source identifier based on the player's team, message type, and optional channel name.
doc.overview: This function determines the specific chat channel source for a given bot by first checking the message type to distinguish between global channels (like World) and team-specific channels. If the message type is CHAT_MSG_CHANNEL, it attempts to fetch the channel from the ChannelMgr associated with the bot's team; if the channel does not exist or the manager is unavailable, it returns SRC_UNDEFINED. For other message types such as whispers, says, or emotes, it directly maps the type to its corresponding source without requiring a channel lookup.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot whose team context is used for team-specific channels.

params.name: type
params.desc: The type of chat message (e.g., CHAT_MSG_CHANNEL, CHAT_MSG_WHISPER) determining the lookup logic.

params.name: channelName
params.desc: Optional string name of the channel to look up if the message type is CHAT_MSG_CHANNEL; ignored otherwise.

doc.returns: ChatChannelSource::SRC_* enum value indicating the source (e.g., SRC_WORLD, SRC_SAY) or SRC_UNDEFINED on failure.
doc.notes: The function relies on ChannelMgr::forTeam() which may fail if the bot's team has no active channels. Callers should check for SRC_UNDEFINED to handle missing channel configurations.

doc.summary: Determines if a player is within a specific distance threshold based on their level and map location.
doc.overview: This function checks whether a player's current position is within a calculated distance limit relative to a given location. The distance bound varies dynamically: it defaults to 10,000 units for levels above 4, but tightens to 500 or 2,500 units for lower-level players (levels 1-4 and 5-10 respectively). If the player is in a startup phase, the function compares the location against the player's initial spawn position; otherwise, it uses the player's current map ID.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose level and position are being evaluated.

params.name: loc
params.desc: The WorldLocation representing the target point or area for distance calculation.

params.name: fromStartUp
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating if the player is in a startup phase, affecting whether the initial spawn position is used instead of the current position.

doc.notes: The function returns true if the player's level exceeds 16 or if they are within the calculated bound; otherwise, it returns false. It relies on global state via sObjectMgr for startup phase calculations.

doc.summary: Returns true if the provided spell family name matches a specific class's healing flag configuration and the input flags are compatible.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a given spell belongs to a valid healing category by checking against predefined flag sets for Druid, Paladin, Shaman, and Priest classes. It constructs a union of expected healing flags based on the spell family name and performs a bitwise AND operation with the provided `spellFalimyFlags` to verify compatibility. The result is true only if the input flags contain all necessary bits required by the spell family's healing configuration.

params.name: spellFamilyName
params.desc: The identifier for the spell family (e.g., SPELLFAMILY_DRUID, SPELLFAMILY_PALADIN). Must be non-zero to proceed.

params.name: spellFalimyFlags
params.desc: A flag value representing the specific healing properties or conditions of the spell being evaluated.

doc.notes: The function returns false if `spellFamilyName` is zero. It relies on hardcoded bitmasks for each class; any spell family not explicitly listed will result in a return value of false.

doc.summary: Converts a class identifier to its corresponding spell family name.
doc.overview: This function maps the input class ID (cls) to a predefined spell family constant using a switch statement. If the provided class matches one of the standard game classes, it returns the specific spell family associated with that class; otherwise, it defaults to SPELLFAMILY_GENERIC.

params.name: cls
params.desc: The class identifier (uint8) representing the character's class.

doc.returns: SPELLFAMILY_* constant corresponding to the input class, or SPELLFAMILY_GENERIC if the class is unrecognized.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure cls is a valid game class ID before invoking this function to avoid receiving the generic spell family.

doc.summary: Registers a callback to be executed after a specified delay by adding it to the bot's event queue.
doc.overview: This function schedules a user-provided callable to run asynchronously within the ShadowAI bot system. It constructs a LambdaEvent object wrapping the provided callback and injects it into the bot's event manager, calculating its execution time based on the requested delay in milliseconds. The event will be processed by the game loop once the delay has elapsed.

params.name: callback
params.desc: A std::function<void()> representing the action to execute after the delay.

params.name: delayMs
params.desc: The time in milliseconds to wait before executing the callback.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the callback is valid and does not capture non-copyable objects unless moved correctly. The delay is relative to the current game tick; if the bot is paused or running in a different context, timing may vary.

Otherwise, it checks a configuration setting to determine if the current map restricts healer DPS and toggles the bot's strategy accordingly.

doc.overview: This function initializes a performance monitor for the full tick cycle and adjusts an internal delay timer using the provided elapsed time. It checks if the AI can be updated before proceeding to call the internal update routine, ensuring thread safety through a yield operation.

doc.summary: Sets the time interval for the next artificial intelligence check in ShadowAI.
doc.overview: This function configures the delay before the AI system performs its subsequent logic evaluation. By updating the internal state variable, it allows developers to dynamically adjust how frequently the AI reacts to player actions or environmental changes without restarting the server process.

params.name: delay
params.desc: The duration in milliseconds to wait before the next AI check occurs.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure thread safety if invoked from multiple contexts, as it modifies internal state. Edge cases include setting a delay of zero, which may cause immediate re-evaluation depending on the AI loop implementation.

doc.summary: Increments the timer for the next artificial intelligence check by a specified number of milliseconds.
doc.overview: This function adds to the internal counter that determines when the AI will perform its next state evaluation. It is typically used to pause or accelerate AI reactions based on game events such as player actions or environmental changes. The delay accumulates and is applied to the next scheduled check rather than resetting the timer.

params.name: delay
params.desc: The number of milliseconds to add to the next AI check interval.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the delay value is non-negative. The function modifies internal state but does not trigger immediate AI behavior; the effect is realized on the next call to the AI check routine.

doc.overview: This function takes a comma-delimited string representation of integers and converts each token into a uint32_t, storing them in the reference list. params.desc: A string containing comma-separated integer IDs (e.g., "1,2,3").

params.name: list
params.desc: A reference to a vector that will be populated with the parsed uint32_t values.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure 'value' is not empty and contains only valid integers; invalid tokens may cause undefined behavior during parsing. Edge cases include leading/trailing whitespace or non-numeric characters which will likely result in conversion errors.

doc.summary: Parses a comma-separated string of integer IDs and inserts them into the provided set.
doc.overview: This function takes a string containing space or comma-delimited integers and populates a reference set with those values. params.name: value
params.desc: A string containing one or more comma-separated integers representing the IDs to be added.

params.name: set
params.desc: A reference to a set of uint32_t where the parsed integer IDs will be inserted.

doc.notes: The function assumes the input string is well-formed; it does not handle empty strings or non-numeric characters gracefully, potentially causing undefined behavior during atoi conversion. Callers should ensure the input format matches expectations.

doc.summary: Splits a comma-separated string into individual elements and appends them to the provided list, skipping empty entries.

params.name: value
params.desc: The input string containing comma-separated values to be parsed.

params.name: list
params.desc: A reference to the target list where the parsed strings will be appended.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure 'value' is not null and that 'list' has write access. The function assumes standard ASCII or UTF-8 encoding for string splitting.

doc.overview: This function performs a binary search to determine whether a specific account ID is present within the internal `randomBotAccounts` vector. It returns true if the ID is found and false otherwise, allowing callers to quickly verify membership without iterating through the entire list manually.

params.name: id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the account to search for within the random bot account list.

doc.notes: Assumes `randomBotAccounts` is a sorted vector; callers should ensure data integrity before relying on binary search performance. Returns false if the ID does not exist or if the container is empty.

doc.summary: Checks if a given quest ID exists within the list of random bot quests.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a specific quest identifier is included in the collection of quests that can be randomly assigned to bots. It performs a linear search through the internal vector of quest IDs and returns true if a match is found, otherwise false.

params.name: id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the quest to check for inclusion in the random bot quest list.

doc.notes: Caller should ensure 'id' is a valid uint32 value. Performance is O(n) relative to the size of randomBotQuestItems.

doc.summary: Determines if a player is prohibited from engaging in PvP based on their zone and area identifiers.
doc.overview: This function evaluates whether the specified zone or area falls under PvP restrictions by checking three distinct conditions. It first verifies if the provided zone ID is in a prohibited list, then checks if the area ID is restricted, and finally ensures that the area ID itself does not correspond to a prohibited zone. The result of this logical combination dictates the availability of PvP activities for players within those specific geographic boundaries.

params.name: zoneId
params.desc: The unique identifier for the current game zone being evaluated.

params.name: areaId
params.desc: The unique identifier for the specific area within the zone being evaluated.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure both inputs are valid non-zero identifiers before invoking this function to avoid undefined behavior. Edge cases include scenarios where an area ID matches a prohibited zone ID, which the third condition explicitly handles.

doc.summary: Checks if a given zone ID is present in the list of PvP-prohibited zones.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a specific zone identifier matches any entry in the global `pvpProhibitedZoneIds` container. It performs a linear search to verify membership and returns true only if an exact match is found, otherwise it returns false.

params.name: id
params.desc: The numeric identifier of the zone to check for PvP prohibition status.

doc.notes: Relies on the global `pvpProhibitedZoneIds` container being initialized; callers should ensure this state is set before invoking. Performance degrades linearly with the number of prohibited zones.

doc.summary: Checks if a given area ID is present in the list of PvP-prohibited areas.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a specific area identifier matches any entry in the global vector `pvpProhibitedAreaIds`. It performs a linear search through the vector to verify membership and returns true only if an exact match is found. The operation relies on the pre-populated configuration data for prohibited zones.

params.name: id
params.desc: The numeric identifier of the area to check against the prohibited list.

doc.notes: Caller should ensure `pvpProhibitedAreaIds` is initialized before calling; returns false for invalid or non-existent IDs. Performance is O(n) relative to the size of the prohibited list.

doc.summary: Checks if a specific map ID is restricted for healer DPS based on global configuration.
doc.overview: This function determines whether the current server configuration enforces restrictions on healer damage per second (DPS) for the provided map. It performs a linear search through a list of restricted map IDs to verify if the given mapId matches any entry in the configuration.

params.name: mapId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the game map to check.

doc.notes: Returns true if healer DPS is restricted and the mapId exists in the restricted list; otherwise returns false. Caller should ensure mapId is valid before calling to avoid undefined behavior with invalid iterators.

doc.overview: This function attempts to open a log file specified by fileName in the given mode, handling both existing and new files. If the file already exists in the internal logFiles map, it closes the previous handle before opening a new one; otherwise, it initializes a new entry. The function retrieves the configured logs directory from sConfigMgr to construct the full path before invoking fopen.

params.desc: The name of the log file to open or reset.

params.name: mode
params.desc: A string pointer containing the file opening mode (e.g., 'r', 'a', 'w').

doc.summary: Logs a formatted string to a specified file or standard output while ensuring thread safety and proper file handling.
doc.overview: This function safely writes a variadic string message to a log file identified by fileName, falling back to standard output if the file cannot be opened. It utilizes a mutex lock to prevent race conditions during concurrent logging operations and ensures all data is flushed to disk before returning.

params.name: fileName
params.desc: The name of the log file to write to; if the file does not exist or cannot be opened, the function falls back to stdout.

params.name: str
params.desc: A format string that defines how the subsequent arguments should be interpreted and written to the output.

doc.side_effects: I/O, global state (logFiles map), mutex lock/unlock
doc.notes: Callers must ensure str is not null. The function modifies the logFiles global state by opening or appending to files. Edge case: if fileName is empty or invalid, behavior depends on isLogOpen implementation.

doc.summary: Parses a semicolon-delimited string of world buff configurations from the shadow AI config manager and populates the global worldBuffs vector.

It iterates through each entry, splitting it into metadata (five specific IDs) and spell IDs, converting them to integers, and storing valid combinations in the worldBuffs container while logging errors for malformed or incomplete data.

doc.summary: Splits a string into a vector of substrings based on repeated occurrences of a specified pattern.
doc.overview: This static utility function divides an input string into multiple segments wherever the provided pattern appears. It handles empty strings by returning an empty vector and processes the remaining text after each match to find subsequent occurrences. The implementation assumes the pattern is non-empty and does not account for overlapping matches.

params.name: str
params.desc: The input string to be split.

params.name: pattern
params.desc: The delimiter string used to separate the input into segments.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the pattern is not empty to avoid infinite loops or unexpected behavior. The function does not handle overlapping patterns; for example, if the pattern is 'aa' and the string is 'aaa', it will split into ['a', 'a'] rather than capturing the overlap.

doc.summary: Parses a class-specific talent tab link string into an ordered list of talent IDs based on the Shadow class configuration.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the optimal talent order for a specific class by filtering the global talent store to only include talents matching the provided class mask. It then sorts these talents within each of the three available tabs according to their row and column indices, prioritizing talents with higher levels before appending them to the result vector.

params.name: cls
params.desc: The numeric identifier for the character class (e.g., Shadow) used to filter talents via the class mask.

params.name: tab_link
params.desc: A hyphen-separated string containing level indicators for each of the three talent tabs, where '-' denotes an empty tab and '0' skips a specific level.

doc.notes: The function relies on global stores (sTalentStore, sTalentTabStore) and assumes valid class identifiers; it returns an empty vector if the input tab link is malformed or contains no valid levels.

doc.summary: Parses the temporary pet talent order for a specific spec and tab link by filtering global talent entries based on spec masks and excluding hardcoded IDs, then sorting them into an ordered list.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the sequence of spells available for a player's temporary pet talents by iterating through the global talent store. It filters entries to include only those matching the provided spec bit mask while explicitly excluding specific talent IDs (2201, 2208, 2219, 2203). The resulting spell list is sorted by row and column, then processed against the input tab link string to construct a final ordered vector of talent configurations.

params.name: spec
params.desc: A uint32 value where the bit corresponding to the desired spec must be set for talents to be included.

params.name: tab_link
params.desc: A string containing digit characters representing the level of each talent in the desired order; non-digit characters are ignored.

doc.notes: The function relies on global stores (sTalentStore, sTalentTabStore) and performs no I/O or network operations. It returns an empty vector if the spec mask matches no talents or if the tab link is invalid.

doc.summary: A singleton configuration class defining all boolean flags, integer thresholds, and vector lists used to control Shadow AI bot behaviors, combat logic, and communication settings.
doc.overview: The ShadowAIConfig class serves as the central repository for game server-side bot parameters, utilizing a static instance pattern to ensure global accessibility. It aggregates numerous boolean switches that toggle specific bot capabilities such as IC buffs, PvP prohibitions, and auto-save mana features alongside extensive numeric thresholds for combat distances, health states, and cooldowns. Additionally, it manages complex behavioral vectors including lists of random accounts, quest items, and spell IDs, as well as weighted teleportation probabilities to various faction cities.
doc.notes: The class relies on a static instance method for access; callers must ensure thread safety when modifying the singleton state. Many parameters define ranges (min/max) for randomized bot behaviors, and some fields like 'randomBotMapsAsString' require parsing into vector formats before use.

doc.summary: Reads a complete line of text from a network socket into a provided string buffer and returns the extracted line.
doc.overview: This function continuously reads data from a socket until it encounters a newline character, accumulating the input into the supplied buffer. Once the newline is found, it extracts the line preceding it into the output string pointer and clears the buffer for the next read operation. The function handles end-of-file conditions by returning false on error or EOF.

params.name: sock
params.desc: A socket pointer representing the network connection from which data is being read.

params.name: buffer
params.desc: A pointer to a std::string that serves as the temporary storage for accumulating incoming bytes until a newline is detected.

params.name: line
params.desc: A pointer to a std::string where the extracted line of text (excluding the newline) will be stored upon successful completion.

doc.notes: Returns false if an error occurs or end-of-file is reached; otherwise returns true. The caller must ensure the buffer pointer is valid and non-null before calling.

doc.summary: A RAII guard class that ensures a bot's initialization state is unique and thread-safe by managing a shared mutex lock.
doc.overview: The BotInitGuard class implements the Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII) pattern to prevent multiple bots from being initialized simultaneously. It acquires an exclusive lock on a static shared mutex upon construction, marking the bot as active only if it has not been initialized yet, and releases this lock in the destructor regardless of whether the bot was successfully added to the initialization set.

doc.notes: Callers should use this guard to ensure only one instance of a bot is initialized at a time. The IsLocked() method returns true if the guard has not yet acquired the lock or if the bot was already active.
